newsitem.title: HONDURAS: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, May 12 - Puerto Cortes - Five vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers/general cargo, 2 discharging (1 fertiliser, 1 wheat/soya). 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 in ballast, 1 ro-ro. 22 Vessels due of which 1 passenger ferry, 12 to discharge/load containers/general cargo, 5 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 to load timber, 1 to discharge fuel oil. Slight congestion expected on Mondays and Fridays due to accumulation of container and ro-ro vessels. Puerto Cortes - Five vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers, 2 discharging (1 urea, 1 sbm/srw/corn). 8 Vessels awaiting berths of which 5 to discharge/load containers, 2 to discharge (1 steel coils, 1 fertiliser), 1 passenger vessel. 11 Vessels due of which 6 to discharge (5 bananas, 1 rice), 4 to load/discharge containers, 1 to discharge fertiliser/load sugar.

MEXICO, May 13 - All ports working normally. Tampico - Five vessels in port of which 1 minerals, 1 coke, 1 asphalt, 1 fuel. Altamira - Three vessels in port of which 2 containers, 1 under repair. Veracruz - 11 vessels in port of which 3 sugar, 1 iron, 2 containers, 3 corn, 2 pipes. Manzanillo - Nine vessels in port of which 2 fruit, 3 containers, 2 general cargo, 1 cars, 1 under repair. Coatzacoalcos - 16 Vessels in port of which 9 chemicals, 7 oil tankers.

UNITED STATES, May 12 - Jersey City, NJ - Two vessels in port. Port Newark, NJ - One vessel in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Five vessels in port. Perth Amboy, NJ - No vessels. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. Cartaret, NJ - Two vessels in port. All northern New Jersey ports working normally with no congestion or delays. Baltimore, MD - Port working normally. Eight bulkers, 3 container vessels, 2 ro-ros, 2 auto vessels, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo vessels, 2 cable vessels on stand-by. 4 Vessels in repair yard, 3 bulkers awaiting berths of which 1 to discharge sugar, 1 to discharge ore, 1 under arrest. Hampton Roads, VA - Six general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 1 general cargo vessel anchored waiting to load, 5 bulkers berthed loading coal. 1 Tanker discharging crude oil, 1 bulker loading scrap, 2 berthed under repair. 2 Vessels berthed discharging cement, 1 bulker berthed discharging minerals.Honolulu, HI - Honolulu harbour - 1 Container vessel, 4 tugs and barges berthed. Honolulu anchorage

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - Dundalk terminal - No congestion anticipated this week. Clear C/D canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Consol Coal - Average waiting time 3 days. Liquid bulk facilities - Working normally with no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No vessels due at either shipyard river coal terminal or grain elevator over the next week. No delays expected at tanker terminals. Allied terminal - Expects vessels on 12, 13, 15 and 17/5. Charleston and Wando terminal - Expected to be light. Dredging continues in main channel with no navigational problems.

Miami, FL - No congestion or delays expected this week at either Miami or Port Everglades. Traffic expected to be normal. New York, NY - Congestion in New York anchorage Stapleton but none in Bayridge. Congestion at tanker terminals and sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - Southern Coal pier - 13 Vessels due during this week. Dominion terminal - 8 Vessels due. Pier IX terminal - 5 Vessels due during the next week. Cargill - No vessels due during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals - Working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals - All working normally. All channels are open, with prevailing depths available.

Philadelphia, PA - No congestion in the ports of Philadelphia, Camden, or Wilmington. No dredging/repairs/navigational problems. Savannah, GA - Garden City - Terminals are expecting a steady week for the entire period. Ocean terminals are forecasting heavy congestion early in the week but slowing by Thursday. East Coast terminal - Expecting a moderate week with no delays expected. Colonial Marine terminals - Bulk clay facility expects long delays. Savannah sugar refinery has two vessels due for the upcoming week. All bulk liquid facilities are working nmally with no congestion expected. Navigation remains normal. As the weather warms, afternoon thunderstorms May cause some downtime on weather-sensitive cargoes.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Cargill grain elevator, Houston public grain elevator or Farmland grain elevator. Galveston - Congestion exists in some private terminals for break bulk cargo and oil/chemical terminals. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rains occurring which May cause delays in cargo operation, especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for the season. River stage at 12.5 feet and expected to go down to 12.4 ft. Normal transit times can be expected. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Based on these drafts, we would advise all vessels to maintain sufficient airdraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi river. High river will cause delays in ship movements and to vessel transit times. Present max permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 45 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 44 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - The pacific N.W. grain movements have slowed significantly this past month, but are expected to continue through June and in to July. There are currently 7 grain vessels in the Columbia river district, of which 5 loading and 2 waiting. Average waiting period 1-2 days at occupied grain berths, immediate berthing available at 2 elevators. Coos Bay, OR - Two lumber vessels and one nickel discharging vessel made up the schedule this week at Coos Bay's waterfront. Expect the next two weeks to make this up with numerous chip vessels and various lumber and log vessels. Roseburg dock wood-chip facility will be extremely busy, with vessels competing for berth space. Honolulu, HI - Medium traffic expected for Honolulu and Barber's Point harbours for the forthcoming week. No bunkering delays are expected due to weather. Long Beach, CA - Coal terminals - Moderately busy, no congestion. The new R.P.L. mega terminal constructed on Terminal island, is scheduled to open up next week.
